message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta.** In the United States, “noise complaints” are handled by the city’s police department or code‑enforcement office rather than a “local council” as in some other countries. Here’s how you can do it in Atlanta: | Step | What to Do | Where to Go / Who to Call | |------|------------|---------------------------| | **1. Identify the source of the noise** | Determine whether it’s a residential, commercial, or public‑space issue. | — | | **2. Contact the City of Atlanta Police Department (APD)** | Most noise complaints are processed through APD’s 311 service or the Noise Complaint Unit. | • **Phone:** 404‑656‑3111 (24 h)
• **Website:** [Atlanta Police Department – 311](https://www.atlantapd.org/311) | | **3. File an online complaint** | Use the city’s online portal to submit a noise complaint form. | • **Link:** [City of Atlanta Online Services – Noise Complaint](https://www.atlanta.gov/311) | | **4. If the noise is from a business or construction site** | You may also file a complaint with the City’s Code Enforcement Division. | • **Phone:** 404‑656‑3111 (same as 311)
• **Email:** code.enforcement@atlantaga.gov | | **5. Follow up** | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy for any follow‑up calls or emails. | — | ### Quick Tips - **Time matters:** Noise complaints are most effective when reported promptly—ideally within 24–48 hours of the disturbance. - **Provide details:** Include the exact location, time, and nature of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs). - **Use the 311 app:** If you have a smartphone, download the City of Atlanta 311 app for instant reporting and status updates. - **Check the noise ordinance:** Atlanta’s noise ordinance (Title 10, Chapter 1 of the Atlanta Municipal Code) defines permissible noise levels and hours. Knowing this can help you describe the violation accurately. ### Bottom Line Yes, you can report a noise complaint in Atlanta. Use the City of Atlanta Police Department’s 311 line or the online portal to file your complaint, and you’ll be connected to the appropriate enforcement agency.
